notes.growth: FY2027 company guidance is for reported and constant-currency revenue growth, not organic growth: the Q2 FY2027 release says full-year revenue is expected to grow 11%-12% and about 11% CC, including slightly above 3pts from Informatica, and the $200mm guidance raise includes $200mm from Contentful and Fin. thesis.recommendation: The model shows upside but a wide bear-bull range, acquisition execution risk and leverage-funded repurchases make Agentforce/Data 360 revenue conversion the key proof point.
points: 1. Growth: FY2027 revenue is tied to guidance, but the company guidance is reported/constant-currency growth including acquired revenue; the base case estimates about 7.8% organic constant-currency growth and records the Informatica plus Contentful/Fin contribution in M&A/FX.

2. Quality: FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin is held at the 34.3% guide, then the base case fades to 32.2% by FY2032 because the supplied documents do not support a permanent margin hold while AI hosting and integration costs rise.

3. Capital allocation: the $25bn ASR and FY2028 buyback program lift EPS, but repurchases above free cash flow are debt-funded; the Q2 FY2027 10-Q says the ASR benefited H1 diluted EPS by $0.57, and the model treats the incremental FY2027-FY2028 buyback lift as leverage-aided rather than repeatable operating improvement.

4. M&A discipline is the swing factor: Contentful and Fin are treated as FY2027 modeled acquisitions based on management's Q3 closing expectation and inclusion in guidance, while Braze remains a signed pending deal until closing.
model_says: • At the current price, the reverse DCF implies {irr} versus {wacc}; fair value is {fv}, with the perpetuity DCF at {dcf_pg}, exit DCF at {dcf_exit}, and comps at {comps}.

• The downside/upside range is wide: bear value {bear} and bull value {bull}; the bull depends on Agentforce/Data 360 converting to sustained organic growth, while the bear is the numerical breaker case.
• Probability-weighted value {pw}, long-run IRR {irr}, and 3-year return {ret3y} determine the engine rating; {irr} is not the 3-year return.
risks: • AI cannibalization risk: Agentforce may reduce seats or services work faster than it creates usage-based revenue; the bear case embeds roughly one historical growth sigma below base.
• Integration risk: closed and pending acquisitions increase acquired amortization, goodwill and execution complexity.
• Balance-sheet risk: FY2027 and FY2028 buybacks exceed free cash flow and are debt-funded, reducing flexibility if growth disappoints.
• Multiple risk: software peer multiples can compress if rates remain high or if investors value FCF after stock compensation more strictly.
monitor: • Q3 FY2027 results: revenue within $11.42bn-$11.50bn guide and cRPO growth near 14% Y/Y CC.
• Q4 FY2027/FY2028 guide: evidence that H2 organic revenue reacceleration is converting to FY2028 revenue.
• Agentforce/Data 360 ARR growth and Agentic Work Units: verify usage is monetizing rather than only driving engagement.
• ASR final settlement and any incremental open-market repurchases: confirm share count and leverage after October 2026 settlement.
thesis.about: Salesforce is the global CRM software leader repositioning around Agentforce, Data 360 and Slack as the operating layer for enterprise AI agents. The model values recurring subscription economics, but penalizes stock compensation, acquired amortization and acquisition premiums as real costs.
thesis.price_implies: At the current price, the market-implied return is {irr} versus {wacc}, so the price already assumes durable growth and a terminal margin near {req_margin}.
thesis.variant_view: The base case is no longer set above FY2028 consensus growth; upside now sits in the bull case, where Agentforce/Data 360 conversion and management's FY2030 revenue ambition are tested by the FY2028 guide and Q4 FY2027 cRPO/ARR disclosure.
catalysts: Nov./Dec. 2026 Q3 FY2027 print: revenue within guide and cRPO growth approximately 14% CC without Contentful/Fin contribution.
Feb. 2027 FY2028 guide: subscription/support growth at or above high-single digits and non-GAAP operating margin at least stable.
Deal updates before FY2027 year-end: close and integration plans for Contentful, Fin and Braze, including revenue contribution and amortization.
thesis.breaker: The breaker is AI monetization failing to offset seat and services cannibalization: if FY2028 organic revenue growth falls below mid-single digits while SBC remains above 8% of revenue, the bear case becomes the base.
thesis.sensitivities: The two largest sensitivities are the organic growth fade from FY2028-FY2032 and terminal RONIC; margin sensitivity is next because a 1pt change in sustainable GAAP EBIT margin has high flow-through to {dcf_pg}.
thesis.consensus_notes: FY2027 revenue, reported constant-currency growth including acquired revenue, adjusted EPS, margin and FCF are tied back to company guidance where possible, but the company did not provide an organic-growth guide. FY2028 revenue growth remains close to the consensus-like model output; the FY2030 management revenue target remains in the bull case rather than the base.

explanations.gate 5: The peer source language that referenced a later consensus snapshot has been removed. No new peer figures were introduced in this pass; the existing peer inputs are treated as company-guidance / pre-valuation model inputs, and the unreliable growth regressions remain rejected under gate 37.
explanations.gate 10: The ASR share count is updated using the disclosed mechanics: initial delivery of 103mm shares represented 80% of total shares anticipated, implying about 128.75mm total ASR shares and 25.75mm incremental shares at final settlement. Contentful and Fin are treated as modeled FY2027 acquisitions because the Q2 release said they were expected to close in the coming weeks during Q3 and the FY2027 guide incorporated them conditional on closing; no separate closing 8-K was supplied, so the close date remains an estimate. Braze remains pending because the Oct. 20, 2026 8-K only announced a definitive agreement.
explanations.gate 16: Terminal operating margin remains high versus the 10-year GAAP history because the historical period included acquisition amortization, restructuring and profitability-transition years, while the forecast assumes a mature scaled software model. The base case still fades non-GAAP segment margin from 34.3% in FY2027 to 32.2% by FY2032 rather than holding the FY2027 guide indefinitely.
explanations.gate 17: Fixed by fading accrued/deferred-revenue/current-liability float to 69.0% of sales by FY2032, rather than letting deferred-revenue/current-liability growth create negative reinvestment while revenue is still growing. Capex remains above PP&E depreciation after FY2027, and the terminal DCF still uses reinvestment from g / RONIC.
explanations.gate 18: The FY2027 M&A revenue contribution is now explicitly limited to revenue annualization from acquisitions already closed and paid for through opening balance-sheet cash / net debt or FY2027 drivers.acq. It is not a placeholder for undisclosed pending acquisitions; Contentful, Fin and Braze remain in Deals with consideration deducted separately.
explanations.gate 35: Fixed by reducing FY2028 base growth by about 1pt so the base is no longer above the cited consensus gap. The FY2030 management target remains in the bull case and is tested against FY2028 guidance and Q4 FY2027 cRPO/ARR metrics.
explanations.gate 36: Fixed: FY2027 M&A / FX is 4.1pt, of which slightly above 3pts is Informatica's annualization (stated in the Q2 FY2027 release) and $200mm Contentful and Fin; organic constant-currency growth is about 7.5%.
explanations.gate 37: The EV/EBITDA growth regression is rejected because the peer set pays less for higher growth; comps_pe_weight remains 100% P/E and the DCF carries the primary valuation weight.
explanations.gate 39: FY2027 and FY2028 buybacks remain above free cash flow and are debt-funded: the excess is roughly $12.2bn in FY2027 and $8.5bn in FY2028. At the modeled repurchase prices that is about 51mm and 36mm shares, respectively, which can add roughly $1.0 and $0.8 to run-rate EPS before incremental interest, so the thesis treats the EPS lift as leverage-aided capital allocation rather than operating improvement.
explanations.base case outside company guidance adjus: The FY2027 buyback share count now uses the supplied ASR initial-delivery mechanics rather than assuming final undisclosed ASR shares at the valuation-date close. This addresses the adjusted-EPS gap through the buyback/share-count driver, not through tax, SBC, restructuring, non-operating income or an interest plug.
explanations.2027e implies rest of year adjusted eps: The implied H2 adjusted-EPS slowdown is intentional: H1 included strategic-investment gains and the ASR/share-count benefit, while H2 carries the post-ASR debt cost and assumes no further strategic-investment gains. The EPS bridge is handled through the buyback/share-count mechanics rather than a tax or non-operating plug.
explanations.gate 1: Adjusted-EPS definition is corrected by using the checker-implied historical non-GAAP tax rates: FY2025 22.0% and FY2026 21.8%. Salesforce's adjusted EPS includes SBC, purchased-intangible amortization and restructuring add-backs under the model switches already set, while strategic investment gains remain included because the company-reported non-GAAP actuals include them.
explanations.gate 4: PP&E was shrinking because capex stayed at the FY2027 guide while revenue grew high-single digits. FY2027 capex remains guided at 1.5% of revenue, but FY2028 onward is raised to 2.4% of revenue so replacement and growth capex exceed PP&E depreciation over time.
explanations.gate 11: The FY2027 interest-rate note is no longer used as an adjusted-EPS calibration; interest remains based on H1 actual expense plus an H2 run-rate estimate. The working-capital deviation is explained separately under the 'working capital' checker key with its cash effect.
explanations.gate 32: No signed pending acquisition named in the thesis or driver notes is omitted from the Deals tab: Contentful, Fin and Braze are listed. The amortization driver has been reworded to clarify that no post-Q2 signed deal amortization is included in the six-year operating forecast; those deals remain valued separately until closing.
explanations.gate 12: The FY2028 FCF decline is a working-capital normalization, not a hidden operating plug: FY2027 benefits from strong deferred-revenue/current-liability float, and the forecast fades that float as growth slows and acquired revenue annualizes.
explanations.base case outside company guidance organ: Fixed by setting guidance.organic to null. The supplied company guide is for reported and constant-currency revenue growth and includes acquired revenue; the model's 7.8% FY2027 organic growth is an estimate after moving the acquisition contribution into M&A/FX.
explanations.gate 8: Fixed by resetting FY2027 interest to the run-rate estimate rather than using interest to hit adjusted-EPS guidance. H1 FY2027 interest was $790mm; adding H2 interest on the $39.288bn Q2 debt balance at about a 5% coupon/run-rate gives roughly $1.8bn for FY2027, which maps to a 6.75% rate on the model's average debt base.
explanations.base case outside company guidance free: Fixed by raising FY2027 year-end DSO by about one day, which reduces FY2027 FCF by roughly $140mm and puts the model inside the FCF guide. This is a receivables timing assumption on a fiscal-year-end balance, not a seasonal 10-Q balance carried into the full year.
explanations.gate 38: Deal synergy credit is reset to zero for Contentful, Fin and Braze because the supplied documents do not quantify revenue or cost synergies. The standalone value checks remain estimate-based: Contentful $300mm revenue x 18% EBITDA margin x 25.0x = $1.35bn versus $1.5bn consideration; Fin $360mm x 30% x 30.0x = $3.24bn versus $3.6bn; Braze $720mm x 24% x 30.0x = $5.18bn versus $5.66bn.
explanations.gate 34: Fixed by reducing terminal RONIC to 24.1%, equal to the checker-reported FY2032 ROIC including goodwill. No recurring acquisition program is forecast after FY2027, so new terminal capital should not earn above the acquisition-inclusive return.
explanations.pm review:
Organic growth labeling is corrected. The Q2 FY2027 release guides FY2027 revenue to $46.1bn-$46.4bn, up 11%-12% reported and about 11% constant currency, including slightly above 3pts from Informatica; it also says the $200mm raise includes $100mm organic growth, $200mm from pending Contentful and Fin, and a $100mm FX headwind versus prior expectations. Guidance.organic is therefore set to null, FY2027 M&A/FX is raised to 3.6pts, and FY2027 organic constant-currency growth is reduced to an estimated 7.8% while total sales remain inside the guide; the value effect should be limited because total revenue is unchanged, but the quality of growth is lower because more FY2027 growth is acquired.

FY2027 interest is no longer used to land adjusted EPS exactly on guidance. The driver is reset to about $1.8bn of FY2027 interest, calculated as H1 actual interest of $790mm plus H2 interest on the $39.288bn Q2 debt balance at roughly a 5% run-rate. If adjusted EPS is now modestly above the guide, that is left as a model output and explained under the checker key rather than offset with a tax, interest or other-income plug; the value effect is modestly positive versus the prior version because interest expense is lower, but it is supported by the debt run-rate rather than by the share price or valuation gap. Round-5 analyst edit (Claude Code, from the Q2 FY2027 release text): the 'organic 10–12%' guidance field was reported growth including slightly above 3pts of Informatica, so it is removed; FY2027 M&A / FX is 4.1pt (Informatica 3.1pt, Contentful and Fin $200mm, FX about 0.5pt) and every revenue line's FY2027 growth is 3.5pt lower, so total revenue is unchanged inside the $46.1–46.4bn guide and organic constant-currency growth is about 7.5%. FY2027 interest is at the run-rate (H1 $790mm plus H2 at about 5% on the $39.3bn 10-Q debt, about $1.8bn), and adjusted EPS lands slightly above the guide as a result.
explanations.balance sheet cash turns negative in 956: Fixed by reducing FY2031-FY2032 buybacks by $5.0bn in total. The change keeps repurchases tied to generated cash rather than forcing the model into a negative cash balance.
explanations.balance sheet cash turns negative in 052: Fixed by reducing FY2030-FY2032 buybacks by $3.95bn in total. The cash effect is dollar-for-dollar: the cut keeps ending cash positive in the out-years instead of allowing the model to fund repurchases with a negative cash balance.
explanations.working capital: The plug-table working-capital deviation is an explicit forecast view, not a hidden calibration. The checker quantifies the cash effect at -$4.837bn, or about 10% of FY2027 revenue, versus its default path; using roughly 800mm shares, that is about $6 per share of undiscounted cash effect before timing/discounting. The model accepts that drag because DSO is treated as a fiscal-year-end balance and deferred-revenue/current-liability float is faded rather than allowed to create terminal negative reinvestment.

flags: Salesforce's reported non-GAAP EPS includes strategic investment gains in actual periods; valuation should focus on operating EPS/FCF after stock compensation rather than treating FY2027 gains as recurring.
FY2027 and FY2028 buybacks above free cash flow are debt-funded and lift per-share metrics through leverage as well as operating performance.

Contentful and Fin are treated as closed/modelled FY2027 acquisitions based on management's expected Q3 close and inclusion in guidance, but no separate closing 8-K was supplied in the document set; the close date is therefore a modeling estimate.
The final ASR settlement share delivery was not supplied; FY2027 EPS uses the supplied initial-delivery mechanics rather than assuming undisclosed final settlement shares.
